blocks.x: A working build of Data & Lakehouse inside Healthcare & Life Sciences: the operating context that shapes it, the services sequenced through the method, and the deltas we commit to.

In Healthcare & Life Sciences, data, analytics & lakehouse is the substrate tower: pipeline modernization, lakehouse architecture on databricks and snowflake, streaming and event-driven decisioning, executive bi, master data and cataloging, predictive analytics, and data products that generate revenue. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: data engineering & pipeline modernization, lakehouse architecture & migration, real-time streaming & event-driven decisioning — delivered on Dataq Forge and Dataq Nexus with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: Interoperability gaps despite FHIR mandates
Imaging, genomics, claims and social determinants live in separate estates; exchange compliance is achieved technically but decision support still reads silos.
Trial recruitment and RWE pipelines manual
Protocol eligibility matching against EHR data remains chart-review work; real-world evidence assemblies take months per study.
Clinician burden and documentation debt
Physicians spend hours daily on notes, orders and inbox; burnout drives attrition. Documentation AI exists but stalls on integration with the EHR and on compliance sign-off.

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: HL7 FHIR / TEFCA-style exchange and HL7 FHIR / TEFCA-style exchange. Interoperability obligations for access and exchange. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

The cadence below is the standard pattern for this capability, and it does not flex by account. Weeks 1–2 are measurement only: we lock the current metric with your team and both sides sign it before a line of build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver a bounded pilot — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a named control owner on your side. Weeks 9–12 turn what worked into runbooks, monitoring and enablement, then report the measured delta against the baseline. A missed gate means a documented stop-or-redirect decision, not a quiet extension.
